cases.prompt: Draft the Azure DevOps work item for the request in the input file. For each work item, put a line `Type: <work item type>` first, then give each field as a level-2 Markdown heading followed by its value. Do not run any commands and do not try to create anything in a tracker; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: Chooses User Story, not the Bug the requester asked for, because the export never existed
Description uses As a ..., I want ... so that ... with an Additional Context section
Story points are a Fibonacci value (5 or 8), not the dev lead's 6-7
Acceptance criteria are numbered sections with checkboxes and measurable values (50,000-row cap, 10 seconds)
Iteration path is the current sprint, Sprint 14

assertions.name: story-quality
rubric: The description is one 'As a <persona>, I want ... so that ...' sentence naming the shipping coordinators (or warehouse operations) and the weekly carrier reconciliation benefit
The output says why this is a User Story rather than the Bug requested: the export never existed, so it is missing functionality, not a defect
Acceptance criteria state the 50,000-row cap with the exact blocking message, the 40,000-rows-under-10-seconds target, and that filters and sort order are respected
Nothing listed as out of scope in the input (scheduled or emailed exports, .xlsx, other grids) appears as an acceptance criterion

cases.prompt: Turn the request in the input file into Azure DevOps backlog work. For each work item, put a line `Type: <work item type>` first, then give each field as a level-2 Markdown heading followed by its value. Do not run any commands and do not try to create anything in a tracker; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: Chooses Issue (technical work), not the story the tech lead asked for
Description uses We need ... to ..., not As a developer
Splits the 20-point estimate into at least two estimated items along the independently deployed API and worker, each Fibonacci and at most 13
Acceptance criteria use the measurable facts: 412 unit and 38 integration tests, 0 high scan findings, p95 at or below 340 ms
Iteration path is next sprint, Sprint 23

assertions.name: no-vague-criteria
assertions.pattern: (?im)^\s*([-*]|\d+\.)\s+(\[[ xX]\]\s+)?[^\n]*(?<![\"'\u201c\u2018])\b((everything|all (existing )?(functionality|features)|existing (functionality|features))\s+(should\s+)?(still\s+)?(works?|continues? to work)\b|works correctly|(is|are|be|runs?) faster\b(?! than \d)|performance is (good|better|improved|the same|unchanged)|code is clean)

assertions.name: issue-quality
rubric: The work is split into at least two Issues along independently deliverable parts (for example the API with Dispatch.Core, and the route worker), each estimated at 13 points or fewer
Acceptance criteria cite concrete checks from the input: 412 unit tests and 38 integration tests passing, 0 high-severity scan findings, and GET /routes p95 at or below 340 ms
Each Issue description begins 'We need ... to ...' and records dependencies such as the shared Dispatch.Core library or the two EF Core query rewrites
No out-of-scope item from the input (.NET 9, queue replacement, rewriting other EF queries) appears as an acceptance criterion

cases.prompt: Write a user story with acceptance criteria for letting customers reset their password from the mobile app.
File a bug in Azure DevOps for the checkout page crashing when the cart is empty, with repro steps and a severity.
How many story points should this backlog item be, and can you tighten its acceptance criteria?
Write the pull request description for my branch that implements AB#5120.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: a PR body for finished work is not a work item.

cases.prompt: Write a spec and implementation plan for the new notifications feature before we start coding.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: a spec and plan under specs/ is not an ADO work item.

cases.prompt: Log two hours in Harvest against the Azure DevOps work item I just finished.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: logging time against a work item is not writing one.
